gc.outfit.title: Outfit
gc.outfit.short: Wear the look of other gear: your character shows the outfit, while stats and attacks stay those of the real pieces.
gc.outfit.body:
At the [[gc.outfit.wardrobe|wardrobe]] you put armor and weapons into your outfit. If you wear a piece whose [[gc.outfit.slots|slot]] in the outfit is filled, your character shows the outfit piece; stats, attacks and effects stay those of the real piece. An empty slot shows the real piece, a slot without a worn piece shows nothing, and you can [[gc.outfit.hide|hide]] armor completely.

Items in the outfit are not in your inventory: they add no [[valheim.stat.carryweight|weight]], stay with you when you die and can only be changed at the wardrobe. All other players see your outfit, even without the mod, because Valheim sends the look like normal equipment; the mod is part of GC Server ([[gc.kern.stufe|level]] 1 “Very vanilla”).

gc.outfit.enabled.title: Outfits and wardrobe
gc.outfit.enabled.short: Server rule for outfits. Off: everyone sees the real gear, and the wardrobe cannot be built.
gc.outfit.enabled.body: This [[gc.serverrules|server rule]] is {gc_outfit_enabled}. When it is off, everyone sees the real gear, the [[gc.outfit.wardrobe|wardrobe]] disappears from the hammer, and at an existing wardrobe you can only take items out; the window is then called “Outfit (off on this server)”. Your [[gc.outfit|outfit]] stays saved and shows again as soon as the rule is on.

gc.outfit.wardrobe.title: Wardrobe
gc.outfit.wardrobe.short: Furniture where you change your outfit; built with the hammer at the workbench from 10 finewood and 10 bronze nails.
gc.outfit.wardrobe.body:
You build it with the hammer under Furniture at the [[valheim.station.workbench|workbench]]. E on the wardrobe opens its doors and your inventory; where a chest would be, you see the 18 [[gc.outfit.slots|slots]] of your outfit in three tables: armor, one-handed weapons, two-handed and ranged. Drag and drop works as with a chest, Shift-click moves a piece into its slot or back into the inventory, and a piece already in that slot swaps with it. The eye next to a slot or a right-click on it [[gc.outfit.hide|hides it]].

The wardrobe itself holds nothing, it does not open inside the area of someone else's ward, and if you walk more than 4 m away, the window closes. You can drag the wardrobe panel by its edge and it stays there; a double click on the edge puts it back beside the inventory.

gc.outfit.slots.title: Outfit slots
gc.outfit.slots.short: 18 slots: six for armor pieces from helmet to belt, twelve for weapon kinds. Tools do not go in.
gc.outfit.slots.body:
The six armor slots take only pieces of their kind. The twelve weapon slots stand for sword, axe, mace, knife, spear, polearm (atgeir), two-handed sword, two-handed axe, two-handed club, bow, crossbow and staff; any weapon fits into them, and it shows as soon as you hold a weapon of that kind. That way a sword in your hand can look like an axe.

Tools such as the pickaxe, cultivator or fishing rod have no slot, and the torch always stays real.

gc.outfit.hide.title: Hiding pieces
gc.outfit.hide.short: The eye next to a slot at the wardrobe hides that piece: your character shows nothing there.
gc.outfit.hide.body: This works for every slot: for armor your character shows nothing there, for weapons a weapon of that kind is invisible in your hand and on your back. A right-click on the slot does the same. While a piece is hidden, the eye is crossed out and the row is grey; a second click shows the piece again. The stats of the worn piece stay, only its look disappears.

gc.outfit.sets.title: Gear sets
gc.outfit.sets.short: Four sets at the wardrobe: armour, hotbar, eight supplies and leash bar, swapped with one click. Currently {gc_outfit_sets}.
gc.outfit.sets.body:
At the [[gc.outfit.wardrobe|wardrobe]], the tabs at the top are **Style** (your [[gc.outfit|outfit]], looks only) and four **sets**. You wear one of them: its tab (green) shows live what you have on you, and whatever you put there goes straight to you, armour and weapons are put on at once. The others stay in the wardrobe. The first is called “Everyday” at first, the others “Set 2” to “Set 4”. Each set shows its **gear** in two tables (armour: head, chest, legs, cape; hands and accessories: right and left hand, belt, trinket), below them the **hotbar** for weapons, tools and supplies and the **supplies** (food, potions and meads, ammo; as many slots as your supply bar, eight per row). The hotbar is Valheim's first inventory row, the supplies are your [[gc.vorratsleiste|supply bar]]. Empty slots show a faint picture of what belongs there.

**Wear** swaps: what lies in your hotbar and your supply bar and what you wear goes into your previous set, the chosen one comes to the same slots and is put on. Whatever lies further down stays with you, as does anything that may not go into the set at its place. With the [[gc.tiere.leashbar|leash bar]] every set has a third table with its five slots, for leashes and whistles only; Wear swaps them with the bar. A leash that is holding an animal never goes into a set and stays with you. If there is not enough room, nothing happens. **Rename** gives a set a name, such as “Melee” or “Mage”.

Sets belong to your character like the outfit: every wardrobe shows them, they weigh nothing and stay when you die. Materials, ore and trophies never go in, otherwise every wardrobe would be a weightless store available at every other wardrobe. If the [[gc.serverrules|server rule]] is off, you can only empty sets.
